Upgrade an existing boosterpak project

Source: R/upgrade.R
upgrade_project.Rd

upgrade_project() brings a project created by an earlier boosterpak version up to date. It repairs the managed .Rprofile startup lines, rewrites the managed boosters/attach.R, materializes missing built-in packs, installs missing workflow packages (renv, pak, and boosterpak) into the project library, and snapshots those packages into renv.lock.

Usage

upgrade_project(root = ".", dry_run = FALSE, snapshot = TRUE, verbose = NULL)

Arguments

root

Project root containing an existing boosters.toml file.

dry_run

Whether to report planned changes without modifying files, the project library, or the active session. Default FALSE.

snapshot

Whether to write workflow packages to renv.lock. With FALSE the upgrade still repairs project files and installs missing workflow packages into the project library, but does not write the lockfile.

verbose

Whether to print the upgrade report. NULL prints in interactive sessions. A dry run prints its report when verbose is NULL.

Value

The upgrade report, invisibly. Its actions, skipped, warnings, paths, and preview fields list what was done, or would be done, and which files are affected.

Details

Run a dry run first. upgrade_project(dry_run = TRUE) changes no files, installs no packages, and restores the session options it touched. It prints the planned actions, a preview of the renv.lock changes, and the files a real run would touch.

The snapshot records the R version that runs the upgrade and the CRAN repository URL in use, so run the upgrade from the R version the project should pin. Package entries installed from Posit Package Manager binaries can carry Repository: RSPM and a Platform field. renv's restore code does not read Platform, and RSPM is only a preference: restore falls back to the repository URLs listed in renv.lock, which also serve Windows and macOS binaries. Use snapshot = FALSE to leave renv.lock unchanged.

A clean real run records the installed boosterpak version in [project].boosters_version in boosters.toml. A run is clean when its report has no warnings. Steps that are skipped on purpose, such as repository configuration disabled by an option or a project without a project renv, do not make a run unclean. A missing renv does, because the workflow packages cannot be repaired without it. A run that is not clean repairs what it can, leaves the record as it was, and reports why. A dry run changes nothing. It lists boosters.toml among the files a real run would touch when that run would record the version.

Review the result with git diff (or your version control) before committing. When an install fails with a GitHub rate limit, or with an HTTP 403 or 429 from GitHub that may be a rate limit, the error includes a hint about supplying a GitHub token. The hint never prints a token value.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
boosterpak::upgrade_project(dry_run = TRUE)
boosterpak::upgrade_project()
} # }
